=== sandbox_help ===
CLI surface for the Linux sandbox helper.

The type name remains `LandlockCommand` for compatibility with existing wiring, but bubblewrap is
now the default filesystem sandbox and Landlock is the legacy fallback.

Usage: codex-linux-sandbox [OPTIONS] --sandbox-policy-cwd <SANDBOX_POLICY_CWD> [COMMAND]...

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]...
          Full command args to run under the Linux sandbox helper

Options:
      --sandbox-policy-cwd <SANDBOX_POLICY_CWD>
          It is possible that the cwd used in the context of the sandbox policy is different from
          the cwd of the process to spawn

      --no-proc
          When set, skip mounting a fresh `/proc` even though PID isolation is still enabled. This
          is primarily intended for restrictive container environments that deny `--proc /proc`

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

strengthen through Aspire references and readiness checks:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code> depends on healthy RabbitMQ.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code> depends on healthy RabbitMQ and healthy DocumentDB.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code> depends on <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code> depends on <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> depends on healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code> depends on healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> has no default startup dependency on <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>, even though <code class=\"notranslate\">AI_SERVICE_URL</code> remains configured.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code> remains optional and has no default dependency.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommended Aspire behavior:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Use resource references and <code class=\"notranslate\">WaitFor</code>-style startup sequencing where available.</li>\n<li>Do not treat process/container running state as application readiness.</li>\n<li>Keep the native validator responsible for final readiness by exercising health endpoints and downstream workflows.</li>\n<li>If a resource becomes ready according to Aspire but fails the product/order/RabbitMQ/DocumentDB workflow, validation must fail.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Ports, Networking, Environment, Redis, and Health Behavior</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Experiment 08A has no Redis component. Redis should not be introduced in 08B.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Accepted endpoint model:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>: container port <code class=\"notranslate\">8080</code>, host endpoint <code class=\"notranslate\">http://127.0.0.1:8080</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code>: container port <code class=\"notranslate\">8081</code>, host endpoint <code class=\"notranslate\">http://127.0.0.1:8081</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: internal port <code class=\"notranslate\">3000</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: internal port <code class=\"notranslate\">3001</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: internal port <code class=\"notranslate\">3002</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: internal AMQP <code class=\"notranslate\">5672</code>; management <code class=\"notranslate\">15672</code> should remain internal unless validation explicitly needs temporary loopback access.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>: internal <code class=\"notranslate\">10260</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>: no exposed ports.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: optional <code class=\"notranslate\">5001</code>, excluded from default PASS; if enabled, bind loopback only.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Accepted environment values to preserve:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS=password</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=rabbitmq</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PORT=5672</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqp://rabbitmq:5672</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_URI=mongodb://documentdb:10260/?tls=true&amp;tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=password</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">AI_SERVICE_URL=http://ai-service:5001/</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_SERVICE_URL=http://order-service:3000/</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=1</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">MAKELINE_SERVICE_URL=http://makeline-service:3001</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=1</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: placeholders only; no real external AI credential in source or committed evidence.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Health behavior to map:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>: Compose uses an OpenSSL TLS connection check against <code class=\"notranslate\">10260</code>. Aspire should model startup ordering with a container resource and validator-level TLS readiness. If a custom AppHost health check can verify TLS without exposing DocumentDB to the host, use it; otherwise document that native validation performs the authoritative DocumentDB readiness check through the application workflow.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: Compose uses <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmqctl status</code>. Aspire should model RabbitMQ as a container and validate readiness through broker health plus <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code> queue evidence and application publish/consume behavior.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: HTTP <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> on <code class=\"notranslate\">3000</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: HTTP <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> on <code class=\"notranslate\">3001</code>; functional readiness also requires DocumentDB connectivity.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: product readiness is validated by <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> and product data through UI proxies; no Compose container healthcheck exists in the accepted baseline.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>: HTTP <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> on <code class=\"notranslate\">8080</code> plus product and order proxy workflows.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code>: HTTP <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> on <code class=\"notranslate\">8081</code> plus product and makeline/order proxy workflows.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>: no HTTP health endpoint; validate identity, running state, configured rates, and effect on workload only after deterministic evidence collection.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: optional HTTP <code class=\"notranslate\">/health</code> when enabled; excluded from default validation.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">.NET and Non-.NET Classification</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">The application services are polyglot and should be treated as containerized services, not .NET projects:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Node.js: <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code> build stages.</li>\n<li>Go: <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>.</li>\n<li>Rust: <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>.</li>\n<li>Python: optional <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>.</li>\n<li>Third-party/container infrastructure: <code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>.</li>\n<li>.NET: AppHost only, plus optional validation helper only if approved. No application service is an in-scope .NET project.</li>\n</ul>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Project References Versus Container Resources</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommendation: represent every required service as an Aspire container resource.</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Use <strong>container resources from Dockerfiles</strong> for <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>, and optional <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>.</li>\n<li>Use <strong>container resources from pinned images</strong> for <code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>.</li>\n<li>Use <strong>no Aspire project references</strong> for the application services, because there are no buildable local .NET service projects and source rewrites are out of scope.</li>\n<li>Use <strong>no external resources</strong> for required core services, because the default PASS criteria must be local and reproducible.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">ServiceDefaults is not appropriate for the application services. It requires source-level .NET service integration, and no service source change is approved or needed. The baseline should document the image default user behavior rather than asserting non-root hardening.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Optional AI Service Classification</h3>\n<markdown-accessiblity-table><table role=\"table\">\n<thead>\n<tr>\n<th>Service</th>\n<th>Role</th>\n<th>Technology</th>\n<th>Default status recommendation</th>\n</tr>\n</thead>\n<tbody>\n<tr>\n<td><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code></td>\n<td>Optional OpenAI-compatible text and image generation backend</td>\n<td>Python/FastAPI</td>\n<td>Exclude from the default PASS criteria; document as optional profile</td>\n</tr>\n</tbody>\n</table></markdown-accessiblity-table>\n<p dir=\"auto\">The upstream README explicitly supports running locally without <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code> when Azure OpenAI or OpenAI credentials are unavailable. The default Experiment 08A PASS criteria should not require any Azure subscription, paid model endpoint, external AI availability, or real API key.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Product-service still has <code class=\"notranslate\">AI_SERVICE_URL=http://ai-service:5001/</code> and exposes <code class=\"notranslate\">/ai/*</code> proxy routes. Store-admin checks <code class=\"notranslate\">/api/ai/health</code> and has UI paths for AI-assisted product descriptions/images. Therefore, default validation must prove that product browsing, product administration without AI generation, storefront checkout, order queueing, makeline processing, DocumentDB evidence, and admin order visibility work without <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>. AI endpoints should be classified as optional expected-unavailable behavior in the core profile, not as ignored breakage.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">No real API key may be committed. If an optional AI profile is later approved, it should use <code class=\"notranslate\">.env.example</code> placeholders and local untracked environment files.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Dependencies and Startup Relationships</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Upstream Compose startup relationships:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code> waits for healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code> waits for healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code> and healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code> depends on <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>, but only with default Compose startup semantics.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code> depends on <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>, but only with default Compose startup semantics.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> waits for healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code> waits for healthy <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code> has no Compose dependency on <code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>, even though it is configured with the AI URL.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code> has no dependency.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Runtime dependencies:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Storefront proxies <code class=\"notranslate\">/api/products</code> to <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service:3002</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">/api/orders</code> to <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service:3000</code>.</li>\n<li>Store-admin proxies product APIs to <code class=\"notranslate\">product-service:3002</code>, makeline order APIs to <code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service:3001</code>, order submission to <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service:3000</code>, and AI endpoints through product-service.</li>\n<li>Order-service declares and publishes to RabbitMQ queue <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code> using host <code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>, port <code class=\"notranslate\">5672</code>, username <code class=\"notranslate\">username</code>, password <code class=\"notranslate\">password</code>.</li>\n<li>Makeline-service consumes RabbitMQ using <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqp://rabbitmq:5672</code>, queue <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code>, AMQP 1.0 receiver address <code class=\"notranslate\">/queues/orders</code>, and local demo credentials.</li>\n<li>Makeline-service stores orders in DocumentDB through <code class=\"notranslate\">mongodb://documentdb:10260/?tls=true&amp;tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true</code>, database <code class=\"notranslate\">orderdb</code>, collection <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code>, username <code class=\"notranslate\">username</code>, password <code class=\"notranslate\">password</code>, auth source <code class=\"notranslate\">orderdb</code>, and TLS with invalid certificate allowed.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Validator implication: after Compose reports containers healthy, validation must still poll application-level readiness through frontend/admin and backend paths because Compose dependency order is not enough to prove functional readiness.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Ports, Networking, and Local Runtime Safety</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Upstream Compose publishes all backend and UI ports to the host without loopback qualification:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">10260:10260</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">15672:15672</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">5672:5672</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">3000:3000</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">3001:3001</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">3002:3002</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">8080:8080</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">8081:8081</code></li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">5001:5001</code></li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">All services join one bridge network named <code class=\"notranslate\">backend_services</code>. Internal DNS names are the Compose service names and must be preserved.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommended local adaptation requiring approval:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Bind user-facing <code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code> to loopback only.</li>\n<li>Expose RabbitMQ management on loopback only if the validator needs host-side management evidence.</li>\n<li>Keep RabbitMQ AMQP, DocumentDB, order-service, makeline-service, product-service, and AI service internal by default unless the approved validator needs a temporary loopback binding.</li>\n<li>Use an Experiment 08-specific Compose project name and resource labels.</li>\n<li>Avoid relying on upstream fixed <code class=\"notranslate\">container_name</code> values for isolation. If implementation keeps them, validation must detect stale or duplicate containers. Prefer removing or replacing fixed <code class=\"notranslate\">container_name</code> entries while preserving service names and internal DNS, because service DNS is application-visible and container names are operational identities.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">This is a deliberate deviation from upstream Compose host exposure and fixed container names. It should be explicitly approved before implementation.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Environment Variables and Runtime Contracts</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Core environment values that must be preserved unless a local adaptation is approved:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_PASS=password</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=rabbitmq</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PORT=5672</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqp://rabbitmq:5672</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_URI=mongodb://documentdb:10260/?tls=true&amp;tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_USERNAME=username</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=password</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">AI_SERVICE_URL=http://ai-service:5001/</code> in upstream Compose. For a no-AI core profile, either preserve this and document optional AI health failures, or approve a local profile-specific value only if product/admin workflows remain equivalent.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDER_SERVICE_URL=http://order-service:3000/</code>, upstream Compose <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=30</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">MAKELINE_SERVICE_URL=http://makeline-service:3001</code>, upstream Compose <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=20</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: Azure/OpenAI environment placeholders only; no real secrets.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">The RabbitMQ and DocumentDB credentials are local demo configuration, not production secrets. They may appear in <code class=\"notranslate\">.env.example</code> and documentation as sample values, but no real credentials or API keys should be committed.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Commands, Entry Points, and Working Directories</h3>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">documentdb</code>: image command <code class=\"notranslate\">--username username --password password</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">rabbitmq</code>: image default command.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR /app</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD npm start</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">makeline-service</code>: runner starts <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD ./main</code>; no explicit runner <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR</code>, binary copied to image root.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">product-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR /app</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD ./product-service</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code>: nginx runner, generated <code class=\"notranslate\">default.conf</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD nginx -g 'daemon off;'</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code>: nginx runner, generated <code class=\"notranslate\">default.conf</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD nginx -g 'daemon off;'</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR /app</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD ./virtual-customer</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR /app</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD ./virtual-worker</code>.</li>\n<li><code class=\"notranslate\">ai-service</code>: <code class=\"notranslate\">WORKDIR /app</code>, <code class=\"notranslate\">CMD uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5001</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Build contexts are source-relative paths from the upstream repository root. Any copied Compose file, wrapper script, or override must preserve project-directory semantics so <code class=\"notranslate\">src/...</code> paths resolve exactly as intended.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Application State and Persistence</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Observed state model:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Product catalog is seeded in product-service memory and resets on product-service restart or recreation.</li>\n<li>Storefront cart is browser <code class=\"notranslate\">localStorage</code>; it is not server-side persisted.</li>\n<li>Orders are stored by makeline-service in DocumentDB database <code class=\"notranslate\">orderdb</code>, collection <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code>.</li>\n<li>Makeline assigns a random numeric <code class=\"notranslate\">orderId</code> during queue consumption and sets status <code class=\"notranslate\">Pending</code>.</li>\n<li>Virtual-worker updates pending orders to <code class=\"notranslate\">Processing</code>; the UI labels non-zero status as completed.</li>\n<li>Upstream Compose does not declare a named DocumentDB volume. Therefore, persistence beyond container lifetime must not be claimed until measured.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Persistence classification to validate after approval:</p>\n<ol dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Service restart: verify whether current-run order remains visible after restarting makeline-service only.</li>\n<li>Compose stop/start without deletion: verify whether current-run order remains visible if containers are stopped and started without removing the DocumentDB container.</li>\n<li>Container recreation: verify whether current-run order survives <code class=\"notranslate\">docker compose up --force-recreate</code> or DocumentDB container recreation.</li>\n<li>Compose down: verify whether state is removed by <code class=\"notranslate\">docker compose down</code> under the approved configuration.</li>\n<li>Optional named volume: evaluate only if approved, because adding durable storage changes upstream semantics and must not be described as equivalent without evidence.</li>\n</ol>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Expected initial assumption: the official Compose baseline likely provides runtime state while the DocumentDB container exists, not a durable-storage guarantee across container deletion.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Deterministic Workload Handling</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">The required core baseline includes <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code>, but their default random behavior can obscure deterministic evidence.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommended approval option:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Preserve both services in the default service set.</li>\n<li>Use a controlled validation mode for deterministic evidence collection:\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>pause or scale <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> during the unique current-run order assertion, then restore it for workload-profile validation; or</li>\n<li>set a documented low fixed <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR</code> and filter by a unique current-run <code class=\"notranslate\">customerId</code>.</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>Prefer an explicit deterministic validator-submitted order with a unique <code class=\"notranslate\">customerId</code> such as <code class=\"notranslate\">aml08-&lt;runId&gt;</code>.</li>\n<li>Discover the assigned order ID by querying makeline/admin/DocumentDB for that unique customer ID because makeline overwrites/assigns <code class=\"notranslate\">orderId</code> randomly.</li>\n<li>Run <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-worker</code> deterministically after the pending-order evidence is captured, or temporarily set <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=0</code> for one-shot processing if approved. Note: upstream <code class=\"notranslate\">virtual-customer</code> exits when <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=0</code>, so do not use zero for it if the service is expected to stay running.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">The validator must not count old orders, seeded data, or random virtual-customer traffic as current-run evidence.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Functional Validation Plan</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommended positive validator sequence after Human Baseline Approval:</p>\n<ol dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Verify pinned source provenance and license.</li>\n<li>Render effective Compose configuration and confirm the approved service set, build contexts, images, ports, env vars, health checks, restart policies, and network.</li>\n<li>Reject stale or duplicate Experiment 08 containers/resources before startup.</li>\n<li>Build application images from the pinned source.</li>\n<li>Start with an Experiment 08-specific Compose project identity.</li>\n<li>Wait for health plus application readiness.</li>\n<li>Confirm expected containers and labels belong to the current Compose project.</li>\n<li>Confirm host exposure is loopback-only and limited to approved endpoints.</li>\n<li>Fetch storefront health and product data through the storefront endpoint.</li>\n<li>Fetch admin health and product data through the admin endpoint.</li>\n<li>Capture pre-operation RabbitMQ queue state and DocumentDB/order state.</li>\n<li>Submit a unique current-run order to the order workflow.</li>\n<li>Confirm <code class=\"notranslate\">order-service</code> accepts the request with expected success status.</li>\n<li>Confirm RabbitMQ queue <code class=\"notranslate\">orders</code> exists and that application publication/consumption behavior changes as expected.</li>\n<li>Confirm makeline consumes the order and writes a DocumentDB record containing the unique customer marker.</li>\n<li>Confirm the current-run order is visible through makeline/admin-facing workflow.</li>\n<li>Process or observe order completion according to the approved virtual-worker behavior.</li>\n<li>Run persistence classification checks without overstating durability.</li>\n<li>Run negative validation.</li>\n<li>Restore, rerun positive validation, clean up, and verify a fresh repeat run.</li>\n</ol>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Negative Validation Plan</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Preferred negative scenario: make RabbitMQ unavailable to the order workflow.</p>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Recommended behavior:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Stop or isolate only the Experiment 08 RabbitMQ resource.</li>\n<li>Run the native validator against the running baseline.</li>\n<li>Expect non-zero exit.</li>\n<li>Require the failure message to identify RabbitMQ/order publication or queue connectivity, not a generic page or process failure.</li>\n<li>Restore RabbitMQ.</li>\n<li>Rerun positive validation successfully.</li>\n<li>Ensure no persistent data corruption or broken environment remains.</li>\n</ul>\n<p dir=\"auto\">A DocumentDB negative test is acceptable if RabbitMQ failure proves unsafe in implementation, but the alternative must still demonstrate a dependency-specific non-zero failure and clean recovery.</p>\n<h3 dir=\"auto\">Kubernetes Versus Compose Differences</h3>\n<p dir=\"auto\">Supporting Kubernetes evidence at the pinned commit shows these notable differences:</p>\n<ul dir=\"auto\">\n<li>Kubernetes uses prebuilt images tagged <code class=\"notranslate\">2.2.0</code> for application services, while Compose builds local images from source.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes exposes <code class=\"notranslate\">store-front</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">store-admin</code> as <code class=\"notranslate\">LoadBalancer</code> services on port 80 targeting container ports <code class=\"notranslate\">8080</code> and <code class=\"notranslate\">8081</code>. Compose binds local host ports directly.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes keeps backend services as <code class=\"notranslate\">ClusterIP</code>; upstream Compose exposes backend ports to the host.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes includes init containers and probes for startup/readiness, especially RabbitMQ waits. Compose uses <code class=\"notranslate\">depends_on</code> health checks for some dependencies and default depends-on semantics elsewhere.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes sets <code class=\"notranslate\">FASTIFY_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0</code> for order-service; Compose does not set it explicitly. The Compose image still starts successfully by upstream design and should remain authoritative for local validation.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes workload rates are <code class=\"notranslate\">ORDERS_PER_HOUR=100</code> for both virtual services; upstream Compose uses <code class=\"notranslate\">30</code> for virtual-customer and <code class=\"notranslate\">20</code> for virtual-worker.</li>\n<li>Kubernetes resources specify CPU and memory requests/limits; Compose does not. DocumentDB state is treated as container-local runtime state owned by the Experiment 08 Compose project.\\n+\\n+Validated lifecycle classification approved by the human operator:\\n+\\n+| Scenario | Classification |\\n+| --- | --- |\\n+| Restart `makeline-service` only | PASS: current-run order remains visible because DocumentDB container state is unchanged. |\\n+| `docker compose stop` then `docker compose start` with the existing DocumentDB container | EXPECTED FAILURE: upstream DocumentDB seed scripts rerun and fail on duplicate `_id` data. |\\n+| Container deletion or recreation | NOT SUPPORTED: durable persistence across DocumentDB container deletion/recreation is not claimed. |\\n+| Clean reset followed by fresh startup and full positive validation | PASS: a clean Compose reset can start the baseline and validate a new current-run order. |\\n+\\n+This classification preserves the approved upstream baseline without adding named volumes, changing the DocumentDB image, patching seed data, or weakening the primary product/order validation. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [store-admin](../store-admin) app.\\n+\\n+It is a simple REST API written with the Gin framework that allows you to process orders from a RabbitMQ queue and send them to a DocumentDB database.\\n+\\n+## Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Go](https://golang.org/doc/install)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+- [MongoSH](https://docs.mongodb.com/mongodb-shell/install/)\\n+\\n+## Message queue options\\n+\\n+This app can connect to either RabbitMQ or Azure Service Bus using AMQP 1.0. To connect to either of these services, you will need to provide appropriate environment variables for connecting to the message queue.\\n+\\n+### Option 1: RabbitMQ\\n+\\n+To run this against RabbitMQ. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy. This will run RabbitMQ 4.x with the Management UI. AMQP 1.0 is supported natively in RabbitMQ 4.0 and later without any additional plugins.\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `makeline-service` directory.\\n+\\n+Set the connection information for the RabbitMQ queue by running the following commands to set the environment variables:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqp://localhost\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Option 2: Azure Service Bus\\n+\\n+To run this against Azure Service Bus, you will need to create a Service Bus namespace and a queue. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+RGNAME=<resource-group-name>\\n+LOCNAME=<location>\\n+\\n+az group create --name $RGNAME --location $LOCNAME\\n+az servicebus namespace create --name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az servicebus queue create --name orders --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+Once you have created the Service Bus namespace and queue, you will need to decide on the authentication method. You can create a shared access policy with the **Send** permission for the queue or use Microsoft Entra Workload Identity for a passwordless experience (this is the recommended approach).\\n+\\n+If you choose to use Workload Identity, you will need to assign the `Azure Service Bus Data Receiver` role to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+PRINCIPALID=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query objectId -o tsv)\\n+SERVICEBUSBID=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query id -o tsv)\\n+\\n+az role assignment create --role \\\"Azure Service Bus Data Receiver\\\" --assignee $PRINCIPALID --scope $SERVICEBUSBID\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the hostname for the Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=$HOSTNAME\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+export USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=true\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you choose to use a shared access policy, you can create one using the Azure CLI. Otherwise, you can skip this step and proceed to [provision a database](#database-options).\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az servicebus namespace authorization-rule create --name listener --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --rights Listen\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the connection information for the Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+PASSWORD=$(az servicebus namespace authorization-rule keys list --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --name listener --query primaryKey -o tsv)\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqps://$HOSTNAME\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=listener\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=$PASSWORD\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+```\\n+\\n+> NOTE: If you are using Azure Service Bus, you will want your `order-service` to write orders to it instead of RabbitMQ. If that is the case, then you'll need to update the [`docker-compose.yml`](./docker-compose.yml) and modify the environment variables for the `order-service` to include the proper connection info to connect to Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+## Database options\\n+\\n+You also have the option to write orders to either DocumentDB or Azure CosmosDB.\\n+\\n+### Option 1: DocumentDB\\n+\\n+If you are using a local DocumentDB container, run the following commands:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=\\\"mongodb://localhost:10260/?tls=true&tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true\\\"\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_USERNAME=username\\n+export ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=password\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Option 2: Azure CosmosDB\\n+\\n+To run this against Azure CosmosDB, you will need to create the CosmosDB account, the database, and collection/container. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+Run the following command to create the resource group for the Azure CosmosDB Account.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+RGNAME=<resource-group-name>\\n+LOCNAME=<location>\\n+az group create --name $RGNAME --location $LOCNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+Also note that Azure CosmosDB supports multiple APIs. This app supports both the MongoDB and SQL APIs. Choosing one model over the other has significant implications on the authentication method your app can use.\\n+\\n+If you choose to use the MongoDB API, then you are limited to using account keys to authenticate. If you choose to use the SQL API, then you can use Microsoft Entra Workload Identity for a passwordless experience (this is the recommended approach).\\n+\\n+If you choose to use Workload Identity, you will need to do the following tasks:\\n+\\n+1. Assign the built-in `DocumentDB Account Contributor` role to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account.\\n+1. Create a custom role for reading and writing data using Azure RBAC and assign it to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account.\\n+1. Disable the account key authentication method for the CosmosDB account (this is highly recommended).\\n+\\n+You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+# create the cosmosdb account\\n+COSMOSDBNAME=<cosmosdb-account-name>\\n+az cosmosdb create --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --kind GlobalDocumentDB --minimal-tls-version Tls12\\n+\\n+PRINCIPALID=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)\\n+COSMOSDBID=$(az cosmosdb show --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --query id -o tsv)\\n+ROLEID=$(az role definition list -n \\\"DocumentDB Account Contributor\\\" --query \\\"[].id\\\" -o tsv)\\n+\\n+# grant yourself the DocumentDB Account Contributor role\\n+az role assignment create --role $ROLEID --assignee $PRINCIPALID --scope $COSMOSDBID\\n+\\n+# create a custom role for reading and writing data\\n+cat <<EOF > customRole.json\\n+{\\n+    \\\"RoleName\\\": \\\"MyCosmosDBDataContributor\\\",\\n+    \\\"Type\\\": \\\"CustomRole\\\",\\n+    \\\"AssignableScopes\\\": [\\\"${COSMOSDBID}\\\"],\\n+    \\\"Permissions\\\": [{\\n+        \\\"DataActions\\\": [\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/readMetadata\\\",\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sqlDatabases/containers/*\\\",\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sqlDatabases/containers/items/*\\\",\\n+        ]\\n+    }]\\n+}\\n+EOF\\n+\\n+ROLEDEFINITIONID=$(az cosmosdb sql role definition create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --body @customRole.json --query id -o tsv)\\n+\\n+# assign the custom role to yourself\\n+az cosmosdb sql role assignment create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --scope $COSMOSDBID --principal-id $PRINCIPALID --role-definition-id $ROLEDEFINITIONID\\n+\\n+# disable account key authentication\\n+az cosmosdb update --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --disable-key-based-metadata-write-access\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are using the SQL API, you will need to create the database and container. Run the following commands to create the database and container.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY=storeId\\n+az cosmosdb sql database create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --name orderdb --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az cosmosdb sql container create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --database-name orderdb --name orders --resource-group $RGNAME --partition-key-path /$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are using the MongoDB API, you will need to create the database and collection. Run the following commands to create the database and collection.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az cosmosdb create --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --kind MongoDB --minimal-tls-version Tls12\\n+az cosmosdb mongodb database create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --name orderdb --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az cosmosdb mongodb collection create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --database-name orderdb --name orders --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are not using Workload Identity authentication, get the password for the Azure CosmosDB account and save the values to environment variables. Otherwise, skip this step.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+COSMOSDBUSERNAME=$COSMOSDBNAME\\n+COSMOSDBPASSWORD=$(az cosmosdb keys list --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --query primaryMasterKey -o tsv)\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+# if database requires SQL API with Workload Identity\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=\\\"true\\\"\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=cosmosdbsql\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=https://$COSMOSDBNAME.documents.azure.com:443/\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_CONTAINER_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_KEY=$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_VALUE=\\\"pets\\\"\\n+\\n+# if database requires SQL API with account key\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=cosmosdbsql\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=https://$COSMOSDBNAME.documents.azure.com:443/\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_CONTAINER_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=$COSMOSDBPASSWORD\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_KEY=$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_VALUE=\\\"pets\\\"\\n+\\n+# if database requires MongoDB API with Workload Identity\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=true\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=mongodb\\n+export ORDER_DB_LIST_CONNECTION_STRING_URL=https://management.azure.com$(az cosmosdb show -g $RGNAME -n $COSMOSDBNAME --query id -otsv)/listConnectionStrings?api-version=2021-04-15\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders\\n+\\n+# if database requires MongoDB API with account key\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=mongodb\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=mongodb://$COSMOSDBNAME.mongo.cosmos.azure.com:10255/?retryWrites=false\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_USERNAME=$COSMOSDBUSERNAME\\n+export ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=$COSMOSDBPASSWORD\\n+```\\n+\\n+> NOTE: With Azure CosmosDB, you must ensure the orderdb database and an unsharded orders collection exist before running the app. Otherwise you will get a \\\"server selection error\\\".\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+The app relies on RabbitMQ and DocumentDB. Additionally, to simulate orders, you will need to run the [order-service](../order-service) with the [virtual-customer](../virtual-customer) app. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy.\\n+\\n+To run the necessary services, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `makeline-service` directory. Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+docker compose up -d\\n+```\\n+\\n+Now you can run the following commands to start the application:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+go get .\\n+go run .\\n+```\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+[GIN-debug] [WARNING] Creating an Engine instance with the Logger and Recovery middleware already attached.\\n+\\n+[GIN-debug] [WARNING] Running in \\\"debug\\\" mode. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [store-front](../store-front) app.\\n+\\n+It is a simple REST API that allows you to add an order to a message queue that supports the AMQP 1.0 protocol.\\n+\\n+## Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+\\n+## Message queue options\\n+\\n+This app can connect to either RabbitMQ or Azure Service Bus using AMQP 1.0. To connect to either of these services, you will need to provide appropriate environment variables for connecting to the message queue.\\n+\\n+### Option 1: RabbitMQ\\n+\\n+To run this against RabbitMQ. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy. This will run RabbitMQ 4.x with the Management UI. AMQP 1.0 is supported natively in RabbitMQ 4.0 and later without any additional plugins.\\n+\\n+To run the necessary services, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `order-service` directory. Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+docker compose up\\n+```\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `order-service` directory. Then run the following commands:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+cat << EOF > .env\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=localhost\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_PORT=5672\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+EOF\\n+\\n+# load the environment variables\\n+source .env\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Option 2: Azure Service Bus\\n+\\n+To run this against Azure Service Bus, you will need to create a Service Bus namespace and a queue. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az group create --name <resource-group-name> --location <location>\\n+az servicebus namespace create --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name>\\n+az servicebus queue create --name orders --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name>\\n+```\\n+\\n+Once you have created the Service Bus namespace and queue, you will need to decide on the authentication method. You can create a shared access policy with the **Send** permission for the queue or use Microsoft Entra Workload Identity for a passwordless experience (this is the recommended approach).\\n+\\n+If you choose to use Managed Identity, you will need to assign the `Azure Service Bus Data Sender` role to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+PRINCIPALID=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query objectId -o tsv)\\n+SERVICEBUSBID=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query id -o tsv)\\n+\\n+az role assignment create --role \\\"Azure Service Bus Data Sender\\\" --assignee $PRINCIPALID --scope $SERVICEBUSBID\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the connection information for the Azure Service Bus queue and save the values to environment variables.\\n+\\n+Next, get the hostname for the Azure Service Bus queue.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, save the environment variables to a `.env` file.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+cat << EOF > .env\\n+USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=true\\n+AZURE_SERVICEBUS_FULLYQUALIFIEDNAMESPACE=$HOSTNAME\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+EOF\\n+\\n+# load the environment variables\\n+source .env\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you choose to use a shared access policy, you can create one using the Azure CLI. Otherwise, you can skip this step and proceed to [running the app locally](#running-the-app-locally).\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az servicebus queue authorization-rule create --name sender --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --queue-name orders --rights Send\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the connection information for the Azure Service Bus queue.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+\\n+PASSWORD=$(az servicebus queue authorization-rule keys list --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --queue-name orders --name sender --query primaryKey -o tsv)\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, save the environment variables to a `.env` file.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+cat << EOF > .env\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=$HOSTNAME\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=sender\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=\\\"$PASSWORD\\\"\\n+ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+EOF\\n+\\n+# load the environment variables\\n+source .env\\n+```\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+To run the app, run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+npm install\\n+npm run dev\\n+```\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+> order-service@1.0.0 dev\\n+> fastify start -w -l info -P app.js\\n+\\n+[1687920999327] INFO (108877 on yubuntu): Server listening at http://[::1]:3000\\n+[1687920999327] INFO (108877 on yubuntu): Server listening at http://127.0.0.1:3000\\n+```\\n+\\n+## Testing the API\\n+\\n+Using the [`test-order-service.http`](./test-order-service.http) file in the root of the repo, you can test the API. However, you will need to use VS Code and have the [REST Client](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=humao.rest-client) extension installed.\\n+\\n+To view the order messages in RabbitMQ, open a browser and navigate to [http://localhost:15672](http://localhost:15672). Log in with the username and password you provided in the environment variables above. Then click on the **Queues** tab and click on your **orders** queue. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [store-front](../store-front) and [store-admin](../store-admin/) apps.\\n+\\n+This app is a simple REST API that allows you to get a list of products, get a single product, update a product, and add a product.\\n+\\n+Products are loaded into memory and not persisted. So if the app is restarted, the products will be reloaded.\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+The app does not rely on any other services, so you can run it locally without any other services running.\\n+\\n+### Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install)\\n+\\n+### Running the app\\n+\\n+To run the app, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `product-service` directory.\\n+\\n+If you are testing the proxy for ai-service, you will need to run the ai-service container then set the `AI_SERVICE_URL` environment variable to the URL of the ai-service.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export AI_SERVICE_URL=http://ai-service:5001/\\n+export AI_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_SECS=300 # optional; default is 300s for image-generation proxy calls\\n+export PRODUCT_MAX_SIZE_BYTES=10485760 # optional; default is 10 MB for product create/update payloads\\n+docker compose up\\n+```\\n+\\n+Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+cargo run\\n+```\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+    Finished dev [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 0.16s\\n+     Running `target/debug/product-service`\\n+Listening on http://0.0.0.0:3002\\n+[2023-06-28T02:44:47Z INFO  actix_server::builder] starting 16 workers\\n+[2023-06-28T02:44:47Z INFO  actix_server::server] Actix runtime found; starting in Actix runtime\\n+```\\n+\\n+Using the [`test-product-service.http`](./test-product-service.http) file in the root of the repo, you can test the API. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [product-service](../product-service/) and [makeline-service](../makeline-service). If you have access to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI API keys, you can also deploy the [ai-service](../ai-service) to help you generate product descriptions. You should also run the [virtual-customer](../virtual-customer) to simulate customers placing orders to have some order data to work with.\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+### Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\\n+- [Vue CLI Service](https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/cli-service.html)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+- [OpenAI API Key](https://beta.openai.com/docs/developer-quickstart/your-api-keys)\\n+- [Azure OpenAI API Key](https://azure.microsoft.com/products/cognitive-services/openai-service/)\\n+\\n+### Running the app\\n+\\n+The app relies on the [product-service](../product-service), [makeline-service](../order-service), and optionally the [ai-service](../ai-service) along with DocumentDB and RabbitMQ instances running. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy.\\n+\\n+To run the necessary services, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `store-admin` directory.\\n+\\n+If you have access to OpenAI or Azure OpenAI, open the `docker-compose.yml` file, uncomment the `ai-services` block, and add your OpenAI or Azure OpenAI credentials.\\n+\\n+> IMPORTANT: When filling in the values, do not put the value in double-quotes.\\n+\\n+```yaml\\n+environment:\\n+  - USE_AZURE_OPENAI=True # set to False if you are not using Azure OpenAI\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME= # required if using Azure OpenAI\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT= # required if using Azure OpenAI\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY= # required if using Azure OpenAI key auth (not needed with workload identity)\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME=gpt-image-2 # required for image generation\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_API_VERSION=2025-04-01-preview # required for gpt-image-2\\n+  - AZURE_OPENAI_IMAGE_ENDPOINT= # optional override; defaults to AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT\\n+  - OPENAI_API_KEY= # required if using OpenAI (or as fallback for Azure key auth)\\n+  - OPENAI_ORG_ID= # required if using OpenAI\\n+```\\n+\\n+Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+docker compose up\\n+```\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `store-admin` directory. Then run the following commands:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export VITE_PRODUCT_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:3002/\\n+export VITE_MAKELINE_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:3001/\\n+\\n+npm install\\n+npm run dev\\n+```\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+  App running at:\\n+  - Local:   http://localhost:8081/\\n+  - Network: http://192.168.0.144:8081/\\n+\\n+  Note that the development build is not optimized.\\n+  To create a production build, run npm run build.\\n+```\\n+\\n+Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8081/`. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [product-service](../product-service/) and [order-service](../order-service). The app is extremely simple in that it only has a cart and a order submission button. When the order submission button is clicked, the cart is emptied and the order is sent to the order service. Currently there is no order checkout pages to collect any customer information.\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+### Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en/download/)\\n+- [Vue CLI Service](https://cli.vuejs.org/guide/cli-service.html)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+\\n+### Running the app\\n+\\n+The app relies on the [product-service](../product-service) and the [order-service](../order-service) and the rabbitmq instance running. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy.\\n+\\n+To run the necessary services, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `store-front` directory. Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+docker compose up\\n+```\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `store-front` directory. Then run the following commands:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export VITE_PRODUCT_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:3002/\\n+export VITE_ORDER_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:3000/\\n+\\n+npm install\\n+npm run dev\\n+```\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+  App running at:\\n+  - Local:   http://localhost:8080/\\n+  - Network: http://192.168.0.144:8080/\\n+\\n+  Note that the development build is not optimized.\\n+  To create a production build, run npm run build.\\n+```\\n+\\n+Open a browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8080/`. It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [order-service](../makeline-service) to simulate customers submitting orders over a period of time.\\n+\\n+## Running the app locally\\n+\\n+### Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Rust](https://www.rust-lang.org/tools/install)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+\\n+### Running the app\\n+\\n+This app relies on the [order-service](../order-service) and the rabbitmq instance running. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy. \\n+\\n+To run the necessary services, clone the repo, open a terminal, and navigate to the `virtual-customer` directory. Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+docker compose up\\n+```\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `virtual-customer` directory. Then run the following command:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_SERVICE_URL=http://localhost:3000/\\n+export ORDERS_PER_HOUR=3600\\n+cargo run\\n+```\\n+\\n+The `ORDER_SERVICE_URL` environment variable is used to tell the virtual customer where to send the order messages. The `ORDERS_PER_HOUR` environment variable is used to tell the virtual customer how many orders to send per hour. We'll set it to `3600`, which is one order per second.\\n+\\n+When the app is running, you should see output similar to the following:\\n+\\n+```text\\n+Orders to submit per hour: 3600\\n+Order submission interval: 1 seconds\\n+Sleep duration between orders: 1s\\n+Order 1 sent at 14.10ms with status of 201 Created. {\\\"customerId\\\":\\\"1358326708\\\",\\\"items\\\":[{\\\"productId\\\":4,\\\"quantity\\\":3,\\\"price\\\":67.659355},{\\\"productId\\\":9,\\\"quantity\\\":2,\\\"price\\\":21.281868},{\\\"productId\\\":9,\\\"quantity\\\":1,\\\"price\\\":51.21942}]}\\n+Order 2 sent at 1.03s with status of 201 Created. {\\\"customerId\\\":\\\"1888758279\\\",\\\"items\\\":[{\\\"productId\\\":8,\\\"quantity\\\":4,\\\"price\\\":56.293404},{\\\"productId\\\":7,\\\"quantity\\\":4,\\\"price\\\":58.618687},{\\\"productId\\\":4,\\\"quantity\\\":2,\\\"price\\\":19.681084}]}\\n+```\\n\\\\ No newline at end of file\\n@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@\\n+version: \\\"3.7\\\"\\n+services:\\n+  rabbitmq:\\n+    image: rabbitmq:4.3.2-management-alpine\\n+    container_name: rabbitmq\\n+    restart: always\\n+    environment:\\n+      - RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER=username\\n+      - RABBITMQ_DEFAUL…187227 chars truncated…up -d rabbitmq >/dev/null\\n+rabbitmq_deadline=$((SECONDS + 180))\\n+while true; It is meant to be used in conjunction with the [store-admin](../store-admin) app.\\n+\\n+It is a simple REST API written with the Gin framework that allows you to process orders from a RabbitMQ queue and send them to a DocumentDB database.\\n+\\n+## Prerequisites\\n+\\n+- [Go](https://golang.org/doc/install)\\n+- [Docker](https://docs.docker.com/get-docker/)\\n+- [Docker Compose](https://docs.docker.com/compose/install/)\\n+- [MongoSH](https://docs.mongodb.com/mongodb-shell/install/)\\n+\\n+## Message queue options\\n+\\n+This app can connect to either RabbitMQ or Azure Service Bus using AMQP 1.0. To connect to either of these services, you will need to provide appropriate environment variables for connecting to the message queue.\\n+\\n+### Option 1: RabbitMQ\\n+\\n+To run this against RabbitMQ. A docker-compose file is provided to make this easy. This will run RabbitMQ 4.x with the Management UI. AMQP 1.0 is supported natively in RabbitMQ 4.0 and later without any additional plugins.\\n+\\n+With the services running, open a new terminal and navigate to the `makeline-service` directory.\\n+\\n+Set the connection information for the RabbitMQ queue by running the following commands to set the environment variables:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqp://localhost\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=username\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=password\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Option 2: Azure Service Bus\\n+\\n+To run this against Azure Service Bus, you will need to create a Service Bus namespace and a queue. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+RGNAME=<resource-group-name>\\n+LOCNAME=<location>\\n+\\n+az group create --name $RGNAME --location $LOCNAME\\n+az servicebus namespace create --name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az servicebus queue create --name orders --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+Once you have created the Service Bus namespace and queue, you will need to decide on the authentication method. You can create a shared access policy with the **Send** permission for the queue or use Microsoft Entra Workload Identity for a passwordless experience (this is the recommended approach).\\n+\\n+If you choose to use Workload Identity, you will need to assign the `Azure Service Bus Data Receiver` role to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+PRINCIPALID=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query objectId -o tsv)\\n+SERVICEBUSBID=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query id -o tsv)\\n+\\n+az role assignment create --role \\\"Azure Service Bus Data Receiver\\\" --assignee $PRINCIPALID --scope $SERVICEBUSBID\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the hostname for the Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group <resource-group-name> --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME=$HOSTNAME\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+export USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=true\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you choose to use a shared access policy, you can create one using the Azure CLI. Otherwise, you can skip this step and proceed to [provision a database](#database-options).\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az servicebus namespace authorization-rule create --name listener --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --rights Listen\\n+```\\n+\\n+Next, get the connection information for the Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+HOSTNAME=$(az servicebus namespace show --name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --query serviceBusEndpoint -o tsv | sed 's/https:\\\\/\\\\///;s/:443\\\\///')\\n+PASSWORD=$(az servicebus namespace authorization-rule keys list --namespace-name <namespace-name> --resource-group $RGNAME --name listener --query primaryKey -o tsv)\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_URI=amqps://$HOSTNAME\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_USERNAME=listener\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_PASSWORD=$PASSWORD\\n+export ORDER_QUEUE_NAME=orders\\n+```\\n+\\n+> NOTE: If you are using Azure Service Bus, you will want your `order-service` to write orders to it instead of RabbitMQ. If that is the case, then you'll need to update the [`docker-compose.yml`](./docker-compose.yml) and modify the environment variables for the `order-service` to include the proper connection info to connect to Azure Service Bus.\\n+\\n+## Database options\\n+\\n+You also have the option to write orders to either DocumentDB or Azure CosmosDB.\\n+\\n+### Option 1: DocumentDB\\n+\\n+If you are using a local DocumentDB container, run the following commands:\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=\\\"mongodb://localhost:10260/?tls=true&tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=true\\\"\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_COLLECTION_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_USERNAME=username\\n+export ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=password\\n+```\\n+\\n+### Option 2: Azure CosmosDB\\n+\\n+To run this against Azure CosmosDB, you will need to create the CosmosDB account, the database, and collection/container. You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+Run the following command to create the resource group for the Azure CosmosDB Account.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+RGNAME=<resource-group-name>\\n+LOCNAME=<location>\\n+az group create --name $RGNAME --location $LOCNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+Also note that Azure CosmosDB supports multiple APIs. This app supports both the MongoDB and SQL APIs. Choosing one model over the other has significant implications on the authentication method your app can use.\\n+\\n+If you choose to use the MongoDB API, then you are limited to using account keys to authenticate. If you choose to use the SQL API, then you can use Microsoft Entra Workload Identity for a passwordless experience (this is the recommended approach).\\n+\\n+If you choose to use Workload Identity, you will need to do the following tasks:\\n+\\n+1. Assign the built-in `DocumentDB Account Contributor` role to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account.\\n+1. Create a custom role for reading and writing data using Azure RBAC and assign it to the identity that is running the app, which in this case will be your account.\\n+1. Disable the account key authentication method for the CosmosDB account (this is highly recommended).\\n+\\n+You can do this using the Azure CLI.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+# create the cosmosdb account\\n+COSMOSDBNAME=<cosmosdb-account-name>\\n+az cosmosdb create --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --kind GlobalDocumentDB --minimal-tls-version Tls12\\n+\\n+PRINCIPALID=$(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv)\\n+COSMOSDBID=$(az cosmosdb show --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --query id -o tsv)\\n+ROLEID=$(az role definition list -n \\\"DocumentDB Account Contributor\\\" --query \\\"[].id\\\" -o tsv)\\n+\\n+# grant yourself the DocumentDB Account Contributor role\\n+az role assignment create --role $ROLEID --assignee $PRINCIPALID --scope $COSMOSDBID\\n+\\n+# create a custom role for reading and writing data\\n+cat <<EOF > customRole.json\\n+{\\n+    \\\"RoleName\\\": \\\"MyCosmosDBDataContributor\\\",\\n+    \\\"Type\\\": \\\"CustomRole\\\",\\n+    \\\"AssignableScopes\\\": [\\\"${COSMOSDBID}\\\"],\\n+    \\\"Permissions\\\": [{\\n+        \\\"DataActions\\\": [\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/readMetadata\\\",\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sqlDatabases/containers/*\\\",\\n+            \\\"Microsoft.DocumentDB/databaseAccounts/sqlDatabases/containers/items/*\\\",\\n+        ]\\n+    }]\\n+}\\n+EOF\\n+\\n+ROLEDEFINITIONID=$(az cosmosdb sql role definition create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --body @customRole.json --query id -o tsv)\\n+\\n+# assign the custom role to yourself\\n+az cosmosdb sql role assignment create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --scope $COSMOSDBID --principal-id $PRINCIPALID --role-definition-id $ROLEDEFINITIONID\\n+\\n+# disable account key authentication\\n+az cosmosdb update --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --disable-key-based-metadata-write-access\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are using the SQL API, you will need to create the database and container. Run the following commands to create the database and container.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY=storeId\\n+az cosmosdb sql database create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --name orderdb --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az cosmosdb sql container create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --database-name orderdb --name orders --resource-group $RGNAME --partition-key-path /$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are using the MongoDB API, you will need to create the database and collection. Run the following commands to create the database and collection.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+az cosmosdb create --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --kind MongoDB --minimal-tls-version Tls12\\n+az cosmosdb mongodb database create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --name orderdb --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+az cosmosdb mongodb collection create --account-name $COSMOSDBNAME --database-name orderdb --name orders --resource-group $RGNAME\\n+```\\n+\\n+If you are not using Workload Identity authentication, get the password for the Azure CosmosDB account and save the values to environment variables. Otherwise, skip this step.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+COSMOSDBUSERNAME=$COSMOSDBNAME\\n+COSMOSDBPASSWORD=$(az cosmosdb keys list --name $COSMOSDBNAME --resource-group $RGNAME --query primaryMasterKey -o tsv)\\n+```\\n+\\n+Finally, set the environment variables.\\n+\\n+```bash\\n+# if database requires SQL API with Workload Identity\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH=\\\"true\\\"\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=cosmosdbsql\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=https://$COSMOSDBNAME.documents.azure.com:443/\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_CONTAINER_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_KEY=$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_VALUE=\\\"pets\\\"\\n+\\n+# if database requires SQL API with account key\\n+# set the following environment variables\\n+export ORDER_DB_API=cosmosdbsql\\n+export ORDER_DB_URI=https://$COSMOSDBNAME.documents.azure.com:443/\\n+export ORDER_DB_NAME=orderdb\\n+export ORDER_DB_CONTAINER_NAME=orders\\n+export ORDER_DB_PASSWORD=$COSMOSDBPASSWORD\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_KEY=$COSMOSDBPARTITIONKEY\\n+export ORDER_DB_PARTITION_VALUE=\\\"pets\\\"\\n+\\n+# if database ORDER_DB_LIST_CONNECTION_STRING_URL=https://management.azure.com$(az cosmosdb show -g $RGNAME -n $COSMOSDBNAME --query id -otsv)/listConnectionStrings?api-version=2021-04-15\\n+export Messages are only acknowledged\\n+// after a successful DB write, giving us at-least-once delivery guarantees.\\n+func startConsumer(ctx context.Context, repo OrderRepo) {\\n+\\torderQueueName := os.Getenv(\\\"ORDER_QUEUE_NAME\\\")\\n+\\tif orderQueueName == \\\"\\\" {\\n+\\t\\tlog.Fatalf(\\\"ORDER_QUEUE_NAME is not set\\\")\\n+\\t}\\n+\\n+\\tuseWorkloadIdentityAuth := os.Getenv(\\\"USE_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_AUTH\\\")\\n+\\torderQueueHostName := os.Getenv(\\\"AZURE_SERVICEBUS_FULLYQUALIFIEDNAMESPACE\\\")\\n+\\tif orderQueueHostName == \\\"\\\" {\\n+\\t\\torderQueueHostName = os.Getenv(\\\"ORDER_QUEUE_HOSTNAME\\\")\\n+\\t}\\n+\\n+\\tif orderQueueHostName != \\\"\\\" && useWorkloadIdentityAuth == \\\"true\\\" {\\n+\\t\\trunServiceBusConsumer(ctx, orderQueueHostName, orderQueueName, repo)\\n+\\t} else {\\n+\\t\\trunAMQPConsumer(ctx, orderQueueName, repo)\\n+\\t}\\n+}\\n+\\n+func runServiceBusConsumer(ctx context.Context, hostname string, queueName string, repo OrderRepo) {\\n+\\tfor {\\n+\\t\\tif err := serviceBusConsumeLoop(ctx, hostname, queueName, repo); err != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\tif ctx.Err() != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\treturn\\n+\\t\\t\\t}\\n+\\t\\t\\tlog.Printf(\\\"Service Bus consumer error: %s. Reconnecting in 5s...\\\", err)\\n+\\t\\t\\ttime.Sleep(5 * time.Second)\\n+\\t\\t}\\n+\\t}\\n+}\\n+\\n+func serviceBusConsumeLoop(ctx context.Context, hostname string, queueName string, repo OrderRepo) error {\\n+\\tcred, err := azidentity.NewDefaultAzureCredential(nil)\\n+\\tif err != nil {\\n+\\t\\treturn fmt.Errorf(\\\"failed to get credential: %w\\\", err)\\n+\\t}\\n+\\n+\\tclient, err := azservicebus.NewClient(hostname, cred, nil)\\n+\\tif err != nil {\\n+\\t\\treturn fmt.Errorf(\\\"failed to create service bus client: %w\\\", err)\\n+\\t}\\n+\\tdefer client.Close(ctx)\\n+\\n+\\treceiver, err := client.NewReceiverForQueue(queueName, nil)\\n+\\tif err != nil {\\n+\\t\\treturn fmt.Errorf(\\\"failed to create receiver: %w\\\", err)\\n+\\t}\\n+\\tdefer receiver.Close(ctx)\\n+\\n+\\tlog.Printf(\\\"Service Bus consumer connected to queue: %s\\\", queueName)\\n+\\n+\\tfor {\\n+\\t\\tif ctx.Err() != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\treturn ctx.Err()\\n+\\t\\t}\\n+\\n+\\t\\tmessages, err := receiver.ReceiveMessages(ctx, 10, nil)\\n+\\t\\tif err != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\treturn fmt.Errorf(\\\"failed to receive messages: %w\\\", err)\\n+\\t\\t}\\n+\\n+\\t\\tfor _, message := range messages {\\n+\\t\\t\\t// Unmarshal: Service Bus wraps the JSON as a quoted string\\n+\\t\\t\\tvar jsonStr string\\n+\\t\\t\\tif err := json.Unmarshal(message.Body, &jsonStr); err != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\tlog.Printf(\\\"failed to deserialize message envelope: %s\\\", err)\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\tif deadLetterErr := receiver.DeadLetterMessage(ctx, message, nil); deadLetterErr != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\t\\tlog.Printf(\\\"failed to dead-letter message: %s\\\", deadLetterErr)\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\t}\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\tcontinue\\n+\\t\\t\\t}\\n+\\n+\\t\\t\\torder, err := unmarshalOrderFromQueue([]byte(jsonStr))\\n+\\t\\t\\tif err != nil {\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\tlog.Printf(\\\"failed to unmarshal order: %s\\\", err)\\n+\\t\\t\\t\\tif deadLetterErr := receiver.DeadLetterMessage(ctx, message, nil);
